question: The largest share of the iron in human blood was made in which kind of stellar death?
options: A white dwarf blowing itself apart
A red giant shedding its layers
answer: A white dwarf blowing itself apart. A collapsing giant keeps its iron core, crushed into a neutron star or black hole, and throws out only a little new iron. Each exploding white dwarf forges about half a Sun's mass of it; most estimates credit them with more than half of the Solar System's supply.
move: Where something is made matters less than whether it gets out.
trap: Giants end their lives with iron cores, so they seem the obvious source.
